How spacing makes memories last

This report, written for Ore's tests in the shape ChatGPT's page copies, opens with the main claim: reviews spread over days keep a fact far longer than the same reviews crammed into one sitting.example.org+1

What the studies show

A memory fades along a curve, and each well-timed review flattens it. The model most schedulers use writes recall after ttt days as follows.

R=e−t/SR = e^{-t/S}R

  • Spacing effect: the gap between reviews matters more than their count.

  • Testing effect: pulling an answer from memory beats reading it again.

Test inBest gap

A tiny scheduler

python
def next_gap(gap, ok):
    return gap * 2.5 if ok else 1

The closing advice is plain: review a little each day, and let the gaps grow as the answers come easily.
